{{Ship module infobox}}

The '''Collector Limpet Controller''' is an optional internal module that programmes standard limpets to retrieve eligible objects in space. Collectors can recover cargo canisters, manufactured and encoded materials, salvage, and fragments released by asteroid mining, then return them to the ship's cargo hatch.<ref name="collector">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Collector_Limpet_Controller Collector Limpet Controller], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref>

The controller provides the programming and operating limits. Each deployed drone consumes one limpet from cargo, and several collector controllers can operate at the same time.

== Collection modes ==

A collector's behaviour is determined when it is launched.<ref name="collector" />

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;"
! Launch condition !! Behaviour !! End condition
|-
| An eligible object is targeted || The limpet retrieves that one object at high speed. || It expires immediately after the delivery.
|-
| No eligible object is targeted || The limpet enters autonomous collection, repeatedly retrieving eligible objects within range. || It continues until its lifetime ends, it is destroyed, or the ship leaves it behind.
|}

Targeted mode is useful for a single urgent object. Autonomous mode is normally preferred for [[Mining|mining]] because one limpet can make repeated trips while fragments remain nearby. Current module documentation lists speeds of up to 200 m/s for targeted collection and 60 m/s for autonomous collection.<ref name="collector" />

If no eligible object is available, an autonomous collector waits near the ship until a target enters range or its lifetime expires. Objects marked '''Ignore''' in the Contacts panel are not collected.

== Dedicated-controller classes and ratings ==

Dedicated Collector Limpet Controllers are sold in Classes 1, 3, 5, and 7. Higher classes increase the maximum number of simultaneously active collector limpets from that controller.<ref name="collector" />

{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;"
! Controller class !! Maximum active collectors
|-
| 1 || 1
|-
| 3 || 2
|-
| 5 || 3
|-
| 7 || 4
|}

Rating changes mass, integrity, power draw, operating range, lifetime, and value. The trade-offs are not a simple E-to-A improvement:<ref name="collector" />

* '''D-rated''' controllers are the lightest and provide a 600-second lifetime, but have the shortest range in each class.
* '''B-rated''' controllers provide the longest operating range, with a 420-second lifetime.
* '''A-rated''' controllers provide the longest lifetime at 720 seconds, with less range than the B-rated version.
* '''C-rated''' and '''E-rated''' versions offer intermediate or low-cost combinations of those characteristics.

The module's outfitting panel should be checked for exact mass, power, integrity, range, and price before fitting. Multi-limpet controllers can also programme collector limpets, but their collector limits and specifications belong to the controlling module rather than to the dedicated-controller table above.

== Cargo and refinery interaction ==

The ship must have suitable storage or processing for what a collector returns.

* Cargo canisters require free [[Cargo Rack|cargo capacity]].
* Mining commodity fragments require a powered [[Refinery]] before they can be processed into cargo.
* Engineering materials enter their dedicated material storage and do not occupy cargo racks.
* A full cargo hold, blocked refinery, or full material storage can make an object ineligible even while it remains in range.

Collector limpets do not decide what is valuable and do not make illegal salvage legal. Cargo ownership and local jurisdiction still apply to recovered canisters.<ref name="collector" />

== Mining role ==

Collectors support every ship-based asteroid extraction method:

* [[Laser Mining]] produces a continuing stream of ordinary fragments.
* [[Core Mining]] releases free fragments and exposes deposits after detonation.
* [[Sub-surface Mining]] ejects fragments from successful displacement-missile extractions.
* [[Surface Deposit Mining]] releases individual chunks after abrasion blasting.

A collector is not an extraction tool, prospector, refinery, or cargo rack. It automates retrieval after another mining tool has produced a collectable object.

== Limitations ==

Collectors navigate around nearby geometry but can still collide with asteroids, core fragments, ships, or the ring itself. Fragments trapped close to or inside rock are a common cause of repeated limpet losses. Moving beyond the controller's range or departing the instance also ends collection.

The maximum number of active collectors is per controller and stacks when several controllers are fitted. Launching another limpet after the controller has reached its limit does not create an additional active slot.

== Engineering ==

Collector Limpet Controllers accept Lightweight, Reinforced, and Shielded module modifications.<ref name="collector" />

{{#invoke:Engineers|moduleEngineers|module=Collector Limpet Controller|label=Maximum Collector Limpet Controller grade}}
